Configure the Julia engine used by ctsem

Source: R/ctJuliaBackend.R
ctJuliaSetup.Rd

Prepares the Julia engine (ContinuousTimeSEM.jl) that ships with ctsem. The engine's Julia package dependencies have to be installed, which needs the network on a machine where they are not already present. As with ctJuliaInstall, ctsem asks before downloading in an interactive session, skips the step with a message when the dependencies are already installed, and declines in a non-interactive session unless agree = TRUE or the environment variable CTSEM_JULIA_AGREE=yes is set.

Usage

ctJuliaSetup(
  project = NULL,
  julia_bin = NULL,
  threads = NULL,
  force = FALSE,
  agree = NULL
)

Arguments

project

Optional local ContinuousTimeSEM.jl checkout to use instead of the copy that ships with ctsem. Rarely needed, mainly for development.

julia_bin

Optional Julia binary directory.

threads

Number of Julia threads. Julia fixes this when the session starts, so it takes effect only if no Julia session is running yet, or with force = TRUE, which restarts the session. ctFit's cores cannot exceed it. NULL, the default, starts a session with getOption("mc.cores", 2) threads unless JULIA_NUM_THREADS is set, or with the cores of the call that starts the session if that is more. A number given here is also the most threads used by calls that do not set cores. A fit that asks for more cores than the session has threads says so (see ctFit).

force

Reconfigure an existing Julia session.

agree

TRUE to consent to installing the engine's Julia package dependencies without being asked, FALSE to refuse. NULL, the default, asks in an interactive session and refuses otherwise (see ctJuliaInstall).

Value

A Julia-engine status list, invisibly.

Details

The first call downloads and precompiles the dependencies (roughly 120 MB) and compiles the engine, which takes several minutes. Later sessions reuse both, and the first fit of a new model in a session then takes only seconds longer than later fits. Models with a categorical indicator, or with more than four random effects per subject under the Laplace approximation, compile a little more the first time. ctFit(forcerecompile = TRUE) compiles a heavily state-dependent model for faster gradients, at the cost of a minute or more of compiling.

Pressing Escape (or Ctrl-C) during a julia fit returns to the R prompt at once, and keeps the Julia session and everything it has compiled. Julia stops the interrupted work at its next iteration. Work without iterations, such as compiling for a new model, finishes in the background, and if it is still running when the next julia call starts, that call says so and waits. Escape during that wait stops Julia completely. ctJuliaProcesses lists the Julia processes ctsem has running, including any left by R sessions that have ended, and ctJuliaKill stops them.

If JuliaConnectoR or Julia itself is missing, this offers to install it, as ctJuliaInstall does. Use ctJuliaInstall to set up the backend deliberately, or from a script.

See also

ctJuliaInstall, ctJuliaStatus

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ctJuliaSetup()                         # prepare the engine, asking first
ctJuliaSetup(threads = 8, force = TRUE) # restart the session wider
} # }
